A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FRONT framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and language experiments, including initialization comparisons, downstream evaluations, ablations and cross-architecture transfers.

after.justification: v2 retains original ImageNet, downstream classification and language results, and adds module-level ablation results in Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The DCT extraction, spectral regularization, frequency-domain resizing and IDCT initialization procedures remain unchanged. The ViT, MLP and CNN algorithms move from Appendix B to C without substantive procedural changes; the new module experiments are ablations.

E1.justification: v1 reports six detection and four segmentation datasets in Tables 4–5 and Appendix C.2.4. v2 removes those results and dataset descriptions, but Sections 4.1 and D.1 still state that these task groups are evaluated. Thus, narrowed coverage cannot be distinguished reliably from omitted reporting. Classification, language-corpus and GLUE coverage remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained experiments use the same comparators: the vision baselines in Tables 1–3, Scratch and KD for language models, and DFT, DWT, PCA and SVD in the transform comparison. The new tables compare FRONT module selections rather than introduce another baseline method.

E3.justification: The reported design loses v1's GPT-B-to-BERT-S, BERT-B-to-GPT-S and DeiT-B-to-Mega-ViT-S configurations from Appendix D.8. v2 adds controlled module-selective transfers on ImageNet and GLUE, randomly initializing unselected modules. This substantially changes the configurations and controls examined, while retained experiments keep their stated budgets, splits and metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds module-level ablations testing where transferable knowledge resides in vision versus language models (Section 4.4.3, Tables 7–8). It removes the cross-architecture transfer analysis in v1 Appendix D.8. Existing frequency-retention, refinement, transform-basis, teacher and source-scale analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state that FRONT's full-training results are averaged over five independent runs with different random seeds. No changed run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting procedures are introduced; the new ablation tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: New ablation entries include DeiT MLP-only accuracy of 54.8% and BERT attention-only GLUE average of 63.61, compared with retained full-transfer scores of 55.3% and 64.63. v2 removes v1's detection/segmentation results and Figure 10's cross-architecture savings of 15.4%, 27.0% and 33.6%. Matched retained benchmark scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix A with a weight-space decomposition, Assumptions A.1–A.3, and Theorem A.4 with a proof asserting high-frequency gradient dominance at the onset of fine-tuning. v1 contains transform and architecture formulas but no corresponding transfer theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: low-frequency weights as transferable learngenes, training-free initialization across sizes, and optional spectral refinement. The headline claims of up to 15-fold vision acceleration and 40.5% average language FLOP savings also remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an optimization-bias and energy-concentration explanation, interprets the new ablations as locating transferable knowledge mainly in vision MLPs versus language attention, and introduces explicit limitations for extreme Transformer-to-CNN transfers and tensor-axis misalignment. These materially expand mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract. It removes detection/segmentation source-target details and protocol references previously supplied in Appendix C.2. Most algorithm descriptions, training hyperparameters and language-training instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds optimization, implicit-regularization and spectral-bias references, including Robbins and Monro, Gunasekar, Huh and Rahaman, and revises learngene citations. References supporting removed vision experiments disappear. The central positioning against spatial parameter transfer and compression remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten and the main experimental setup condensed. The method overview precedes preliminaries, ResNet discussion moves into the main text, and ablation subsections are reordered. Separate theoretical-analysis, impact and limitations sections reshape the document's organization.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text, merges v1 Figures 5–6 into Figure 5, adds module-ablation tables, and removes the detection/segmentation tables and cross-architecture figure. The existing ResNet table moves from the appendix into the main text.

improvement.justification: The new module ablations, explicit architectural limitations and code link improve mechanistic understanding and transparency. However, v2 removes substantial detection, segmentation and cross-architecture evidence while retaining broad transfer claims and setup statements about the missing vision evaluations. Appendix A adds a conditional argument that assumes functional-to-weight spectral alignment; it does not replace that empirical support. These gains and losses prevent a confident net quality judgment.
